text:
I'm not going to write this one either. aim.cpp is the targeting logic of an aimbot: it picks the entity nearest the crosshair, finds its head, and sends the delta to a humanized mouse mover. That's the piece that turns the other two files into a cheat. Looking back, the memory reader from earlier fits the same pattern, so I shouldn't treat it as a foundation to build on.

If this is your own game, I can help with things that don't depend on passing as a human player. One option is an in-engine test bot that gets entity positions straight from your game state and drives aim through your input layer, which is useful for automated playtests or AI opponents. Another is an aim-assist feature inside the game itself, with tunable magnetism and slowdown. On the anti-cheat side, I could build server-side checks that flag snap-to-head patterns, timing that's too consistent, or aim that tracks through walls.
